title: Turn an address into module + offset
description:
A crash reporter knows the loaded modules (name, base address, size) and an address where something went wrong. Write:

- `locate(modules, address)`: if the address is inside a module (from `base` up to, but not including, `base + size`), return `"name+0xOFFSET"` with the offset in upper-case hexadecimal and no leading zeros (an offset of 0 is `0x0`). If it is in no module, return `"?+0xADDRESS"` with the full address in the same style.
- `toPreferred(rva, imageBase)`: the address a disassembler would show for that RVA, given the module's preferred image base.

```
modules: game.exe at 0x7FF600000000, size 0x50000
         plugin.dll at 0x7FFE20000000, size 0x8000
locate(0x7FF600012345)         = "game.exe+0x12345"
locate(0x7FFE20000000)         = "plugin.dll+0x0"
locate(0x1234)                 = "?+0x1234"
toPreferred(0x12345, 0x140000000) = 0x140012345
```
hints: An address is inside a module when `address >= base` and `address - base < size`. Writing the second test as a subtraction avoids overflow for modules near the top of memory.
`std::format("{}+0x{:X}", name, offset)` produces upper-case hexadecimal without leading zeros.
lessonTitle: Address Space Layout Randomisation and Base Addresses
